newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: VOLKSWAGEN STRIKE ENDS IN S.AFRICA.
newsitem.headline: VOLKSWAGEN STRIKE ENDS IN S.AFRICA.

text.p: About 4,500 workers at German automaker Volkswagen's plant in South Africa's Eastern Cape returned to work on Monday following three days of protests over the company's cost-cutting measures, a spokesman said.

Volkswagen's Raymond Hartle said worker representatives from the National Union of Metalworkers of South Africa had agreed on Thursday -- before Friday's Human Rights holiday -- that their members would resume normal duty on Monday while talks to try and resolve the impasse continued.
"The strike has ended and the workers are back at work. The plant opened this morning and it is going on normally," he told Reuters.
He said Volkswagen had suffered loses of about 55 million rand in lost turnover from the industrial action at its Uitenhage plant which has a daily output of 320 vehicles.
"The company has lost 55 million rand in turnover and the employees have lost 1.8 million rand in wages. The strike has been illegal," Hartle said.

"What the company has been saying from last week is that once there is a return to work, then we can negotiate on the substantive issues and now that has happened, so negotiations will continue," he added.
The workers downed tools on Tuesday last week protesting against Volkswagen's move to have those who lease its cars contribute to insurance costs.
They had also complained about the stricter enforcement of the company's absenteeism policy and the introduction of stringent quality control measures at the plant's paint shop, the company said.
